CanBeGeneratedInCombat.maps_to: NOT PORTED -- the sim relies on rarity instead (neows_fury.py:378-379)
CanBeGeneratedInCombat.issue: `public override bool CanBeGeneratedInCombat => false` (NeowsFury.cs:15) has no `can_be_generated_in_combat = False` counterpart; the sim's comment says the ANCIENT rarity already keeps it out of `pool_card_ids`. That is true today, so the OUTCOME matches -- but it is a different mechanism, and the flag is the one C# actually exposes: `CardModel.CanBeGeneratedInCombat` (CardModel.cs:642) is read by FilterForCombat regardless of rarity, so any future in-combat generator pointed at a pool that includes Ancients would pick up Neow's Fury in the sim and not in the game. DORMANT with the trigger named. Contrast card/feed, card/hand_of_greed and card/hidden_gem, which set the flag explicitly, and card/disintegration / card/frantic_escape / card/mind_rot, which set the WRONG flag -- three different treatments of one override across six cards.

ctor.rationale: `base(1, CardType.Attack, CardRarity.Ancient, TargetType.AnyEnemy)` (NeowsFury.cs:25-28) == cost 1 / ATTACK / ANCIENT / ANY_ENEMY.

CanonicalVars.rationale: `new DamageVar(10m, ValueProp.Move)` + `new CardsVar(2)` (NeowsFury.cs:19-23) == both numbers, both declared.

OnPlay.issue: Attack first, then the hand-size-capped selection: `Math.Min(Cards.IntValue, CardPile.MaxCardsInHand - Hand.Cards.Count)` (NeowsFury.cs:36) == `min(self._cards, PlayerCombatState.MAX_HAND_SIZE - len(ctx.player.hand))`, with both skipping everything when the result is <= 0 (37 == 399-400), and MaxCardsInHand is 10 on both sides (CardPile.cs:21, player.py:56). The `predicate=lambda c: c is not self` is a CORRECT compensation for the sim's discard-pile limbo, matching card/headbutt. THE SELECTION RANGE IS WRONG. C# passes `new CardSelectorPrefs(prompt, 0, num)` (NeowsFury.cs:39) -- MinSelect **0**, MaxSelect num -- so the player may take FEWER than the cap, or none at all. The sim's `CardSelectCmd.from_pile(..., count=count)` resolves through `CombatState.select_cards`, which clamps `count = min(count, len(candidates))` and then takes exactly that many (combat.py:575-581), with no way to express a range. So the sim cannot decline part of the return. DORMANT: taking fewer cards back is strictly worse play, no replay command encodes a partial selection, and the auto-select shortcut C# would take at `candidateCount <= MinSelect` never fires with MinSelect 0 unless the discard pile is empty (where both sides do nothing). It becomes live for any conformance replay of a run where the player declined. This is the min/max-range half of creature_card_cmds guard N10, recorded at a card site because Neow's Fury is the first unit in the pool whose C# prefs actually use a RANGE rather than a fixed count.

guards.what: the chosen cards are moved with `CardPileCmd.Add(list, PileType.Hand)` in C# (NeowsFury.cs:39) and by direct list mutation in the sim (neows_fury.py:405-407)
guards.issue: The sim pops the chosen cards out of `player.discard_pile` and appends them to `player.hand` in place (neows_fury.py:405-407) instead of routing through a pile-add verb, so nothing fires for the pile transition. C# `CardPileCmd.Add` runs `Hook.AfterCardChangedPiles` (CardPileCmd.cs:635) and enforces `MaxCardsInHand` inside `AddInternal` (the cap is separately enforced here by the `count` computation in OnPlay, so only the hook is dropped). SAME MECHANISM AND SAME VERDICT AS card/anointed's `CardPileCmd.Add` guard (rule 3) -- this is the card-level instance of creature_card_cmds's 'no unified AfterCardChangedPiles' structural finding (docs/audit/seams/creature_card_cmds.md:643-666), recorded here because it is Neow's Fury's own code doing the bypass. DORMANT: the sim has no `after_card_changed_piles` listener at all, so nothing observable is dropped yet. TRIGGER: the first ported model overriding `AfterCardChangedPiles`. Was recorded faithful while its own rationale said "Same structural point as card/anointed's guard" and card/anointed carries `gap`; the report also files it under the DORMANT-GAP family "Direct pile mutation instead of a pile verb" (§5).
